said.t: Israel’s Central Elections Committee has completed counting votes in Tuesday’s parliamentary elections, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc securing 53 seats, opposition parties 48 and Arab parties 19, the Ynet newspaper reported Thursday.
Results from 12,644 polling stations have been entered into the system, totaling 5,589,836 votes, including 5,564,764 valid votes and 25,072 invalid votes, it said.
Netanyahu’s Likud party rose from 26 to 27 seats, while the ultra-Orthodox Shas party fell from seven to six.
Among Arab parties, Ra’am gained one seat, increasing its representation to eight, while the Joint List dropped one to 11.
The two Arab parties, the Joint List and the United Arab List (Ra’am), secured a combined 19 seats, potentially putting them in a pivotal position in negotiations to form the next government.
Netanyahu’s bloc nor the opposition bloc reached the 61 seats required for a majority in the 120-member Knesset.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party remains in the lead following the October 27 parliamentary election, with 97.3% of ballots counted, according to preliminary figures released by the Central Elections Committee (CEC).
Likud is projected to win 27 seats in the 120-member parliament, followed by Yashar, led by Netanyahu’s main opposition rival Gadi Eisenkot, with 21.
It is projected to secure 53 seats, compared with 48 for the opposition.
Arab parties are set to win 19 seats, although neither Likud nor the opposition is expected to be willing to form a coalition with them.
A coalition needs at least 61 Knesset seats to form a government, a threshold no political bloc has yet reached.
The first candidate will have 28 days to form a government, with a possible two-week extension.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc maintained its lead after the final vote count from Tuesday's election with 53 seats in the next Knesset, the Central Elections Committee reported Thursday.
The opposition bloc won 48, it said.Both blocs fell short of the 61 seats needed for a Knesset majority.
B'Yachad, led by Naftali Bennett, is expected to enter with 12 seats.

said.t: The announcement came on Thursday (October 29), as the ECB kept its benchmark deposit rate unchanged at 2.5% amid rising inflation, higher energy prices linked to the Middle East conflict and turmoil in European government bond markets, particularly in France.
Lagarde, 70, has led the ECB since November 2019, having previously served as managing director of the International Monetary Fund.
The deposit rate remained at 2.5%, the main refinancing rate at 2.65% and the marginal lending rate at 2.9%.
Eurozone inflation reached 3.8% in September, almost twice the ECB's medium-term target of 2%, as rising energy costs continued to affect the European economy.

Her decision brings an earlier-than-expected end to a presidency that has spanned the Covid-19 pandemic, Russia's invasion of Ukraine and renewed inflationary pressures linked to the Middle East conflict.
Thailand affirms Middle East evacuation readiness on October 30 Brent ends October up 13.6% as Iran war risks unsettle markets Heavy rain warning for four Thai Gulf coast provinces on October 31
The timing matters for borrowing costs across the 21 countries that use the euro.
Lagarde, 70, made the announcement just before the ECB left interest rates unchanged.

European Council President Antonio Costa said the selection process would start immediately and "proceed without delay." Holger Schmieding, chief economist at Berenberg bank, said leaders would likely seek agreement on all three posts before a summit on December 17-18.
In 2020 the bank deployed 1.35 trillion euros ($1.5 trillion) in bond purchases to keep the COVID-19 pandemic from drying up credit.
Lagarde, 70, was originally scheduled to complete her eight-year term on Oct 31, 2027.
As ECB president, Lagarde leads the bank's governing council, which sets interest rates for the 21 countries using the euro.
Schmieding said they would likely seek an agreement before the European Council summit scheduled for Dec 17-18.

One of the major decisions during her tenure came in 2020, when the ECB launched a 1.35 trillion euro ($1.5 trillion) emergency bond-buying programme to keep credit flowing during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Lagarde's resignation announcement overshadowed Thursday's decision by the ECB to keep its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 2.5%.
The decision came despite annual inflation reaching 3.8%, driven partly by higher oil prices linked to the US-Iran war.
Her successor will be appointed by the European Council in accordance with the nomination process set out in Article 283 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.

4a405d1c46951f84.title: Verdens største kryptobørs ramt af muligt hackerangreb
4a405d1c46951f84.summary: Tidligere medstifter af Binance siger, at sikkerhedsbrist på kryptovalutabørs ligner et hackerangreb.

said.t: Historiens hidtil største tyveri af kryptovaluta fandt sted i februar 2025, hvor der blev stjålet for 1,5 milliarder dollar fra kryptobørsen Bybit.
Binance, der giver brugerne mulighed for at købe, sælge og handle digitale aktiver, har mere end 335 millioner registrerede brugere på verdensplan.
Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what is thought to be the biggest crypto hack on record.
Two analytics firms have attributed the incident, which eclipses a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor.
Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
The company said in 2024 that it has more than $160bn in assets under its custody.
Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they had frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack.

The price of other major cryptocurrencies including Ethereum and Solana also fell sharply.
Et beløb, der svarer til 42,50 milliarder danske kroner, hvilket ifølge analytikeren Aravind Srinivasan fra det førende globale kryptovalutafirma GSR gør det til »det største hack i historien« .

TRM sporer midlerne og advarer sine partnere via Beacon Network.« Analysefirmaet oplyser videre, at FBI tidligere har udpeget den samme hackergruppe som ansvarlig for et Bybit-hackerangreb på 1,5 milliarder dollar i februar 2025.
»Flere træk ved dette angreb svarer til tidligere tyverier med tilknytning til Nordkorea, herunder Bybit-hacket og KelpDAO-hacket i april 2026,« lyder det.

The breach sent cryptocurrency prices lower, triggered $1.5 billion in liquidations and raised fresh concerns over security and customer funds held by major exchanges.

Binance Holdings, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, lost an estimated $6.3 billion to hackers early on Friday, in what has been described as the single biggest theft of crypto on record, exceeding the $1.5 billion stolen from Bybit in February 2025 .
Funds began leaving Binance's hot wallets, which are connected to the internet to process customer withdrawals, at about 12.24am UAE time on October 30.

A single transaction moved roughly 167,464 Ether, worth about $388 million, along with 63 other tokens, to an address created hours earlier and funded through the Tornado Cash mixing service, according to Etherscan data.
Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis estimated the haul at $5.912 billion at the time of the theft.
The stolen assets then spread across the Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron and Ripple networks.
Sådan lyder de første meldinger fra Binance, der er verdens største kryptobørs, og som på godt og vel 20 minutter blev lænset for værdier svarende til 6,3 milliarder dollar.
Bitcoin er fredag eftermiddag 3,4 procent mindre værd end et døgn forinden, mens Ethereum er nede med 4 procent.

His statement came as Arab-led parties emerged with a historic 19 seats in Israel's 120-member parliament, the Knesset, placing them in a potentially decisive position during negotiations over the next government.
According to results reported Friday by Agence France-Presse (AFP), Netanyahu's right-wing and far-right bloc secured 53 seats, eight short of the 61 required for a majority.
His Likud party remained the largest individual faction with 27 seats.
The opposition, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, obtained 48 seats, while the Arab-led Ra'am and Joint List parties collectively secured 19 seats.

Israel's public broadcaster KAN reported Thursday evening that vote counting had been completed, with Netanyahu's bloc securing 53 seats, the opposition Change bloc 48 and Arab parties 19 in the 120-member Knesset.
Neither of the two main blocs reached the 61 seats required for a parliamentary majority.

Ifølge Frankrigs indenrigsministerium har 70.000 mennesker lørdag deltaget i en overvejende fredelig demonstration i Paris.
Klokken 14.00 lød status fra politiet i den franske hovedstad, at 27 personer var anholdt.
En uge tidligere meldte politiet om 217 anholdelser.
På landsplan har omkring 320.000 mennesker indtaget gaderne rundt om i Frankrig, lyder vurderingen fra det franske ministerium.
Der er indsat omkring 70.000 politifolk for at holde ro og orden.

France is deploying 70,000 police officers and gendarmes across the country as authorities brace for another weekend of protests and possible violence over rising living costs, deteriorating public services and growing dissatisfaction with President Emmanuel Macron's government.
17 violence, when rioters looted hundreds of shops and security forces struggled to contain the disorder.
Police have also prohibited access to Place de la Republique and Les Halles, two locations affected by the previous unrest, between 11 p.m. and 6 a.m. on Saturday and Sunday.

With public debt approaching 120% of economic output and borrowing costs rising, the government faces mounting pressure to reduce spending, leaving limited room to accommodate demands for greater investment in education and financial relief for households.
Authorities counted approximately 550,000 demonstrators nationwide on Oct.
17, when widespread looting accompanied the protests.

Italian police also remained on alert following confrontations in Milan, Turin and Bologna, while calls for demonstrations circulated on social media in Belgium, the Netherlands, Austria, Switzerland and Portugal.
Luxury retailers, including Hermes, Louis Vuitton and Burberry, were among the businesses targeted during previous outbreaks of violence.
